notes: Intel publishes no 50-state breakdown; its April 2025 U.S. fact sheet (company-hosted PDF) gives investment figures for its four manufacturing states only (Oregon, Arizona, New Mexico, Ohio), and the newer live usachipmaking page has slightly updated numbers ($65B Oregon, $34.5B Arizona, $17.68B New Mexico) plus state GDP contributions; the fact sheet is used because it is closest to the Dec 2024 snapshot. Cumulative investment and new-project figures are different measures and must not be added. The fact sheet also lists CHIPS Act awards per state (AZ $3.94B, NM $500M, OR $1.86B, OH $1.5B); these are government funding to Intel, not Intel's footprint, and are not recorded. Nationally, the fact sheet says Intel has 45,000 U.S.-based employees (company-published; 10-K total workforce 108,900); not recorded as a row because the U.S. row's source is the 10-K PP&E table. A 2021 third-party study ("Intel's Impacts on the US Economy", FY2019 data) covering AZ, CA, NM and OR exists but is far older than the snapshot and was not used. 10-K Properties gives only square feet: U.S. 38 million (35 owned, 3 leased) vs other countries 32 million; there are no per-state or per-country site counts, and the manufacturing countries are listed without figures, so they appear as sites. Ohio fab completion has been slowed and Germany/Poland projects put on hold (10-K).
